The '''1970 New Zealand National Soccer League''' was the inaugural season of a nationwide [[Round-robin tournament|round-robin]] club competition in [[New Zealand]] football. The league's initial sponsors were [[Rothmans, Benson & Hedges|Rothmans (NZ) Ltd]], and the league was thus commonly known as the '''Rothmans National League'''. Rothmans retained naming sponsorship rights until 1987 when [[Air New Zealand]] took over as principal sponsor.<ref name="Hilton">{{cite book |last1=Hilton |first1=Tony |last2=Smith |first2=Barry |title=An Association with Soccer: The NZFA Celebrates Its First 100 Years |year=1991 |publisher=[[New Zealand Football]] |isbn=978-0473012915}}</ref>{{rp|83}}

==Background==
Plans for a national league had been drawn up in 1963 after increasing calls for such a competition from the late 1950s onwards. Plans were delayed by a full programme of overseas games for the NZFA during 1964, but moves towards a viable national league were put in place with the introduction of three regional leagues for the northern, central, and southern regions of the country in 1968. It was the final standing in these leagues in the 1969 season which were to provide the eight teams to compete in the 1970 national league, with four teams from the Central league, three from the Northern League, and one from the Southern League granted national league spots.<ref name="Hilton"/>{{rp|82-83}} The qualifying sides were as follows:

;Northern League
* [[Mount Wellington (soccer)|Mount Wellington]] (Auckland)
* [[Eastern Suburbs AFC|Eastern Suburbs]] (Auckland)
* [[Blockhouse Bay (soccer)|Blockhouse Bay]] (Auckland)

;Central League
* [[Western Suburbs FC (New Zealand)|Western Suburbs FC]] (Porirua)
* [[Stop Out]] (Lower Hutt)
* [[Gisborne City]] (Gisborne)
* [[Hungaria (soccer)|Hungaria]] (Wellington)

;Southern League
* [[Christchurch United]] (Christchurch)

==Team performance==
The inaugural season was dominated by teams from Auckland and Wellington, each of which had three teams. It was an Auckland side which would finish on top, with favourites and 1969 Northern League champions [[Blockhouse Bay (soccer)|Blockhouse Bay]] triumphant. For much of the season it was to be fellow Queen City side [[Eastern Suburbs (soccer)|Eastern Suburbs]] were the main threat for the title, but both [[Christchurch United]] and [[Mount Wellington (soccer)|Mount Wellington]] performed well in the second half of the season, with neither side losing a game in the home stretch until the last game of the season, the league's first floodlit game, which saw Christchurch beat the Mount at home in an eight-goal spectacular in front of the season's biggest crowd of 3,000.<ref name="Hilton"/>{{rp|84}}

By comparison with the Auckland sides, the Wellington trio had lacklustre seasons. The four teams from the central region filled the lower half of the table, and the gap between them and the top four — in both points and form — was substantial.<ref name="Hilton"/>{{rp|84-85}}

No teams were relegated at the end of the 1970 season, as it was decided to increase the size of the league to ten teams from 1971.
